text: Coffee plantations stand at over 13,000 hectares in the hinterland towns of Senator Ninoy Aquino, Lebak and Kalamansig.
SOCCSKSARGEN had 26,179 hectares planted to coffee in 2022, 79 percent of it in Sultan Kudarat.
source: PSA Regional Office XII, Countryside in Figures, Sultan Kudarat 2023 edition

text: The Department of Agriculture named Sultan Kudarat's coffee industry a top priority, with farm-to-market roads earmarked for coffee areas.
Mindanao farmers dominated the 2026 Philippine Coffee Quality Competition.
Amadeo, the "coffee capital", had 4,790 hectares of coffee in 2019.
source: Philippine Coffee Board, citing the Inquirer

text: Coffee area fell from 5,550 hectares in 2005 to 3,427 in 2014 as farms in Tabuk, Tanudan and Pinukpuk turned to corn.
The Bureau of Soils and Water Management's suitability map lists 396 hectares of existing coffee, led by Atok (66), Buguias (64), Bakun (57) and Bokod (56).
source: BSWM land suitability map, Benguet Robusta

text: A Benguet farmer's lot broke the national record for coffee sold at auction.
